Where it began

Zak Crawley was born in Bromley, in Kent, on 3 February 1998, and went to school at Tonbridge. He played for Kent from the under-11s upwards and came through the county academy, turning out at weekends for clubs such as Sevenoaks Vine. He was 15 when he first turned out for the Kent Second XI.

Winters abroad helped. He played grade cricket in Perth for Wembley Districts and later in Sydney, where he hit a hundred from 42 balls for Sydney Cricket Club, the fastest the competition had seen. Back home his first-class debut came against West Indies at Canterbury Week in 2017, and he made 62. His first hundred, 168 against Glamorgan, arrived in September 2018.

The player

England picked him for the tour of New Zealand in 2019, and he made his Test debut at Seddon Park aged 21. In his eighth Test, against Pakistan in 2020, he turned his first Test hundred into 267, sharing a stand of 359 with Jos Buttler that set a new England record for the fifth wicket. At the time only R. E. Foster had made a bigger first Test hundred for England. That summer earned him a place among Wisden's Cricketers of the Year.

There was plenty more to come. In the first Test of England's tour of Pakistan in 2022 he reached a hundred in 86 balls, at the time the fastest by an England Test opener, and in the 2023 Ashes he was England's leading run-scorer, with 189 at Old Trafford the highlight. By November 2026 he had played 64 Tests and made 3,586 runs at 31.18, with five hundreds and 21 fifties, and had held 70 catches.

What made him special

Crawley was a natural stroke-maker, and when he was going well there were few more pleasing sights in cricket than his drive through the covers. He liked to take the attack to the new ball, and in that 2022 Test in Pakistan he very nearly reached his hundred before lunch on the first day.

The same shot that brought him so many runs was, from time to time, his undoing. A swinging ball outside off stump is a great temptation to a batter who loves to drive, and his runs tended to arrive in bursts rather than a steady stream. When they did arrive, though, they came quickly and in quantity.

Away from the middle

For years his mentor was Rob Key, the former Kent captain, and the two made a habit of meeting regularly through the season to work on his game. Crawley captained England in two one-day internationals against Ireland in 2023, and he was named captain of Sunrisers Leeds for the 2026 season of The Hundred. He also played franchise cricket for London Spirit and for Hobart Hurricanes, scoring a fifty in his first game in the Big Bash.

And finally

In the Caribbean in 2018 he was left stranded on 99 not out for Kent against the Leeward Islands. Most batters would count that a near miss. Crawley seems to have taken it as a reason to make his big hundreds very big indeed.
